brief: Goldman Sachs raises its Fed call to a second 25bp hike in October, having previously expected only a September move, after a more hawkish than expected FOMC meeting, and lifts its peak fed funds range to 4.00-4.25%. It raises 2026 year end 10 year yield forecasts for Treasuries to 4.75% (from 4.40%), Bunds to 3.25% (from 3.00%) and Gilts to 5.00% (from 4.40%), tied to updated Fed, ECB and BoE views. It expects one more ECB hike, in December, to a 2.75% peak. Euro area growth forecasts for 4Q26 and 1Q27 are cut to 0.15% and 0.20%, and peak core and headline inflation forecasts raised to 2.7% and 3.8%, both on a surge in energy prices. Global GDP growth is expected to slow to 2.6% yoy in 2026 on the same Middle East driven energy headwinds, with global core inflation ending the year at 2.8%. China's 2026 GDP forecast is cut to 4.5% from 4.6% on weaker activity data. US growth is put at 2.2% Q4/Q4, core PCE at 3.2% easing near 2% in 2027, and unemployment at 4.2%.
